speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Manpower given the increase in income for the 20th and 30th percentiles of income earners since 2016 (a) when was the qualifying income ceiling for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) last revised using these percentiles as benchmarks; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider raising the WIS income ceiling as well as increasing the WIS payouts from the next financial year to assist low-income workers deal with rising costs of living.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the progress of the review on the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme; (b) whether there are studies being commissioned to find out what is considered a "living wage"; and (c) whether there are studies to consider extending coverage to those who are not in formal employment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme was launched in 2007 as a broad-based measure that raises incomes of lower-income workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: WIS payouts are targeted at those with limited household support, with more going to older workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, a 65-year-old earning $1,200 monthly would receive $300 more each month through WIS.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: WIS is regularly reviewed to ensure the target groups continue to be helped.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Ministry of Manpower is conducting its regular review of the WIS scheme to ensure that it continues to provide meaningful support to lower-income workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will take into account the increases in income over the past few years and announce the results of the review when ready.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Most WIS recipients also receive other forms of Government support to help meet their living needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, WIS is not the only mechanism through which we help our low-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nearly all our WIS recipients receive U-Save rebates and over 90% receive Goods and Services Tax (GST) Vouchers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nearly four in 10 also receive outpatient medical subsidies under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Those with children receive other forms of support if eligible, such as subsidies for childcare and student care.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This approach of going beyond wage supplements, to provide further support based on the varied needs of individuals and families, is more responsive than any "living wage".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is not about handouts and transfers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is about advancing workers to be able to be more productive and higher skilled.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: With better skills, our workers can access better wages and better jobs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Government-funded programmes, such as the Workfare Training Support, Adapt and Grow initiative and SkillsFuture, provide active support to promote jobs and skills upgrading in all sectors of the economy, so that lower-income workers can progress along with the rest of the workforce.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, as a result of these efforts, real wage at the 20th percentile grew faster than at the median.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Like other Singaporeans, our lower-income also have the opportunity to build up assets.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Because very few places in the world – in fact, I do not think you will find one – where low-wage workers own their own homes, are able to build up assets.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We recognise that there are workers not in formal employment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Although their incidence in Singapore is generally low, we are concerned about the risks informal workers face.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, they would have little recourse if their employers failed to make timely payments or compensation for work injury, or if their services were unfairly terminated.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The lack of stability also does not enable planning on the part of the individual and impedes his ability to build up his Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings for home ownership, healthcare and retirement.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We should, hence, avoid unwittingly blurring the difference of such work arrangements for workers, or creating an avenue for employers to have reduced or no obligations for these workers with weak bargaining power.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is also why our focus is to help individuals access formal work arrangements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Through Workforce Singapore (WSG), we seek to bring informal workers back into formal employment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Those in need of financial assistance can also approach the Social Service Offices (SSOs).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members would be very familiar with these, as they have helped many of our low-income Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: SSO officers assess the needs of each family holistically and work together with WSG and the National Trades Union Congress' Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) to facilitate employment assistance where needed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the meantime, informal workers continue to be eligible for other support, such as U-Save rebates, GST Vouchers and CHAS.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I just wanted to explore a little bit on the possibility of actually looking into studies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate the challenges and the concerns in making sure our workers are put into formal employment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But there are concerns for those who are in informal employment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They already have other challenges and, usually, a lot of them are in transition as they are trying to get into better jobs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But in the midst of training, they will need income to assist their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, the reality of life is that they do require some support, although there is some other assistance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is still quite hard to meet their daily demands, especially so with the rising costs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am wondering if we could at least look into it and have some studies in some way where we could use WIS as a motivator so that they can be recruited into formal employment eventually.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Generally, the long-term goal is to work through the other schemes and the SSOs, for example, today, where you have multi-layered support, not just in terms of Workfare.
